title: skills(objectstack-data): teach that a secret or password field is never a filter, sort or search key, only a has-a-value check (Skills-docs follow-up owed by #27477)
body:
domain:devx#1 · sunhaolin · session_017xRBcVy4VXmkQjn2MGeaWk

Filing gate: **③ a maintainer-directed task.** The maintainer, in the PM session `session_017xRBcVy4VXmkQjn2MGeaWk` on 2026-10-29, said (verbatim): 「你应该使用 pm-dispatch 技能审核和落地 pr」. The pm-dispatch review checklist says that a `Skills-docs: follow-up owed` line is filed as a card and rewritten to `#N` before ACCEPT. This card is that follow-up for PR #27477.

Business reason: after #27477, the engine refuses a credential column (`type: 'secret'` / `type: 'password'`) as a filter key, a `{ $field }` comparand, a sort key, an `aggregations[i].filter` key, an expand entry's `where` or `orderBy`, and an import `matchFields` lookup. Each refusal is `400 INVALID_FIELD` for a non-system caller. "Has a value" checks (`null`, `$null`, `$exists`, `$empty`) stay allowed. `skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md` teaches the credential field types but says nothing about querying them. An AI author following the skill can therefore still write a view filter, sort, report or import mapping that the runtime refuses.
Reader: AI agents authoring ObjectStack metadata through the published `objectstack-data` skill.
Dedupe: searched the open and closed issues for "skills credential secret password filter sort"; no card covers this.

## What to add

In `skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md`, near the credential field types, add one rule with a short example:
- a credential column is never a filter, sort, group, search or import-match key;
- the only query a caller may write against it is whether it has a value;
- `searchableFields` should not list it.

Add one eval prompt in the package's eval set that exercises it: ask for a list view filtered by a secret field, and expect the skill to refuse or redirect.

Out of scope: any runtime change, which has shipped in #27477.
